title: Being a local complete intersection over a field is invariant under extension of the field
statement: Let $k$ and $K$ be fields, $\iota:k\to K$ a ring homomorphism (making $K$ a $k$-algebra), and $S$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Then $S\otimes_kK$, a $K$-algebra through $\lambda\mapsto1\otimes\lambda$, is a finite type $K$-algebra, and $S$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field] if and only if $S\otimes_kK$ is a local complete intersection over $K$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00SJ (label lemma-lci-field-change, line 36262); proof lines 36269-36330 (via Lemma 00SC lemma-lci and flatness of k[x]_{p'} -> K[x]_{q'}; or Lemmas lemma-lci-global and lemma-lci-field-change-local)

proof.text: (Presentations.) By [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] there are $n\ge0$ and a surjective $k$-algebra homomorphism $\alpha:P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to S$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; let $I=\ker\alpha$, so $\alpha$ induces a $k$-algebra isomorphism $P/I\cong S$, by which we identify $S$ with $P/I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring] $P$ is Noetherian, so $I=(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ for some $f_1,\dots,f_m\in P$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $P'=K[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $\kappa:P\to P'$ the ring map applying $\iota$ to the coefficients, and $S'=S\otimes_kK$. By [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change] (with $R=k$, $R'=K$, $A=S$, $\pi=\alpha$) the $K$-algebra map $\alpha':P'\to S'$, $x_i\mapsto\alpha(x_i)\otimes1$, is surjective with kernel $I'=(\kappa(f_1),\dots,\kappa(f_m))$, which is the ideal of $P'$ generated by $\kappa(I)$ (each element of $I$ is a $P$-combination of the $f_j$). Hence $S'$ is a finite type $K$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] (first assertion of the lemma), and $\alpha'$ identifies $S'$ with $P'/I'$ as $K$-algebras. Moreover $\alpha'\circ\kappa=j\circ\alpha$ with $j:S\to S'$, $s\mapsto s\otimes1$ (both are ring maps agreeing on $k$ and on the $x_i$). Note that $I/I^2$ is a finitely generated $S$-module (generated by the classes of the $f_j$).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00SJ (lemma-lci-field-change, line 36262), lines 36269-36353: 'Let alpha : k[x_1..x_n] -> S be a presentation with kernel I. proof.text: (The conormal module commutes with the field change.) Let $M=I/I^2$ and $M'=I'/I'^2$, an $S$-module and an $S'$-module. Claim: there is an isomorphism of $S'$-modules $\Theta:M\otimes_SS'\to M'$ with $\Theta((f\bmod I^2)\otimes(1\otimes\lambda))=\lambda\kappa(f)\bmod I'^2$ for $f\in I$, $\lambda\in K$. Proof. Let $\mu:P\otimes_kK\to P'$, $p\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\kappa(p)$, a ring map. By [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change] applied to $A=P$, $\pi=\mathrm{id}_P$, $m=0$ (kernel $(0)$), the $K$-algebra map $\pi':P'\to P\otimes_kK$, $x_i\mapsto x_i\otimes1$, is bijective; $\mu\circ\pi'$ is a $K$-algebra endomorphism of $P'$ fixing every $x_i$, hence the identity [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], so $\mu=\pi'^{-1}$ is bijective. By [lem-weil-field-scalar-extension-exact] the functor $-\otimes_kK$ on $k$-vector spaces is exact; applied to the $k$-subspaces $I^2\subseteq I\subseteq P$ it shows that $I^2\otimes_kK\to I\otimes_kK\to P\otimes_kK$ are injective and that $0\to I^2\otimes_kK\to I\otimes_kK\to M\otimes_kK\to0$ is exact. Under $\mu$ the image of $I\otimes_kK$ is the $K$-span of $\kappa(I)$, and this span is the ideal $I'$ of step 1: it lies in $I'$, and conversely an element $\sum_jh_j\kappa(g_j)$ of $I'$ ($g_j\in I$, $h_j\in P'$) is, writing each $h_j=\sum_t\lambda_{jt}\kappa(p_{jt})$ ($P'$ is the $K$-span of $\kappa(P)$, as it is spanned by the monomials), equal to $\sum_{j,t}\lambda_{jt}\kappa(p_{jt}g_j)$ with $p_{jt}g_j\in I$. In the same way the image of $I^2\otimes_kK$ is the $K$-span of $\kappa(I^2)$, which is $I'^2$ ($I'^2$ is generated as an ideal by the products $\kappa(g)\kappa(h)=\kappa(gh)$, $g,h\in I$). Hence $\mu$ restricts to bijections $I\otimes_kK\cong I'$ and $I^2\otimes_kK\cong I'^2$, and with the exact sequence above it induces a bijection $\beta:M\otimes_kK\to M'$, $(f\bmod I^2)\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\kappa(f)\bmod I'^2$. Finally $M\otimes_S(S\otimes_kK)\cong M\otimes_kK$, $m\otimes(s\otimes\lambda)\mapsto sm\otimes\lambda$ (associativity of the tensor product), and $\Theta$ is $\beta$ composed with it. $\Theta$ is $S'$-linear: $S'$ is generated as a ring by $j(S)$ and $1\otimes K$, and for $p\in P$, $f\in I$, $\lambda\in K$ one has $\Theta((\alpha(p)\cdot(f\bmod I^2))\otimes(1\otimes\lambda))=\lambda\kappa(pf)\bmod I'^2=\alpha'(\kappa(p))\cdot\Theta((f\bmod I^2)\otimes(1\otimes\lambda))$ by $\alpha'\circ\kappa=j\circ\alpha$ (step 1); $K$-linearity is clear.

proof.text: (Primes, dimensions and localized conormal modules.) Let $\mathfrak q\subset S'$ be a prime and $\mathfrak p=j^{-1}(\mathfrak q)\subset S$. (a) By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-field-extension] (with $S_K=S'$, $\mathfrak q_K=\mathfrak q$), $\dim_{\mathfrak p}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S')$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. (b) $j$ maps $S\setminus\mathfrak p$ into $S'\setminus\mathfrak q$, hence into the units of $S'_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], so $S'_{\mathfrak q}$ is an $S_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra and $(M\otimes_SS')_{\mathfrak q}\cong M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{S_{\mathfrak p}}S'_{\mathfrak q}$, $(m\otimes s')/t\mapsto(m/1)\otimes(s'/t)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] (both are $M\otimes_SS'_{\mathfrak q}$). With step 2: $M'_{\mathfrak q}\cong M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{S_{\mathfrak p}}S'_{\mathfrak q}$ as $S'_{\mathfrak q}$-modules. (c) The ring map $S\to S'\to S'_{\mathfrak q}\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ kills $\mathfrak p$ and sends $S\setminus\mathfrak p$ to units, so it factors through $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and $M'_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{S'_{\mathfrak q}}\kappa(\mathfrak q)\cong M\otimes_S\kappa(\mathfrak q)\cong(M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{S_{\mathfrak p}}\kappa(\mathfrak p))\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ by (b) and associativity of tensor products. Since $M$ is a finitely generated $S$-module (step 1), $V=M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{S_{\mathfrak p}}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a finite-dimensional $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-vector space, and a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-basis $v_1,\dots,v_r$ of $V$ gives the $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$-basis $v_i\otimes1$ of $V\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$; so $\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}V=\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}M'_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{S'_{\mathfrak q}}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$.

proof.text: (Only if.) Assume $S$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S'$ be a prime and $\mathfrak p=j^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. By (2) of the definition there is $g\in S$ with $\mathfrak p\in D(g)$, i.e. $g\notin\mathfrak p$, and $S_g$ a global complete intersection over $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lci-conormal-free-rank-codimension] (applied to $k$, $P$, $I$, $S=P/I$ and the prime $\mathfrak p$), $d=\dim_{\mathfrak p}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$ satisfies $0\le d\le n$ and $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is a free $S_{\mathfrak p}$-module of rank $n-d$, say with basis $e_1,\dots,e_{n-d}$. By step 3(b), $M'_{\mathfrak q}\cong M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{S_{\mathfrak p}}S'_{\mathfrak q}$ is generated over $S'_{\mathfrak q}$ by the $n-d$ elements $e_i\otimes1$, and by step 3(a) $n-d=n-\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S')$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lci-conormal-generators-global-complete-intersection] (applied to $K$, $P'$, $I'$, $S'=P'/I'$ (step 1) and the prime $\mathfrak q$) there is $g_{\mathfrak q}\in S'\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $S'_{g_{\mathfrak q}}$ a global complete intersection over $K$. The sets $D(g_{\mathfrak q})$, $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S'$, cover $\operatorname{Spec}S'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] ($\mathfrak q\in D(g_{\mathfrak q})$), and $S'$ is a finitely generated $K$-algebra (step 1), so $S'$ is a local complete intersection over $K$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field] (2).

proof.text: (If.) Assume $S'$ is a local complete intersection over $K$. Let $\mathfrak p\subset S$ be a prime. $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is surjective (each of $k$, $K$ has exactly one prime ideal, $(0)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $\iota^{-1}(0)=0$), so by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-surjective-base-change] (with $R=k$, its $S$ our $K$, $R'$ our $S$) the map $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_kK)\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ induced by $j$ is surjective: there is a prime $\mathfrak q\subset S'$ with $j^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$. By (2) of [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field] there is $g'\in S'\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $S'_{g'}$ a global complete intersection over $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lci-conormal-free-rank-codimension] (applied to $K$, $P'$, $I'$, $S'=P'/I'$ and $\mathfrak q$), $e=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S')$ satisfies $0\le e\le n$ and $M'_{\mathfrak q}$ is free of rank $n-e$ over $S'_{\mathfrak q}$; by step 3(a) $e=d:=\dim_{\mathfrak p}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$. Hence $M'_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{S'_{\mathfrak q}}\kappa(\mathfrak q)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak q)^{n-d}$, and by step 3(c) $V=M_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_{S_{\mathfrak p}}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ has $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-dimension $n-d$. Choose $m_1,\dots,m_{n-d}\in M_{\mathfrak p}$ whose images form a basis of $V=M_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pM_{\mathfrak p}$. $M_{\mathfrak p}$ is a finitely generated module (step 1) over the local ring $S_{\mathfrak p}$ with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], so by [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] $m_1,\dots,m_{n-d}$ generate $M_{\mathfrak p}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lci-conormal-generators-global-complete-intersection] (applied to $k$, $P$, $I$, $S$ and $\mathfrak p$) there is $g_{\mathfrak p}\in S\setminus\mathfrak p$ with $S_{g_{\mathfrak p}}$ a global complete intersection over $k$. The sets $D(g_{\mathfrak p})$, $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}S$, cover $\operatorname{Spec}S$, and $S$ is finitely generated over $k$, so $S$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field] (2).

split_report.summary: Statement and stmt_deps kept (checked against Stacks 00SJ; S (x)_k K for K (x)_k S is the swap). Proof written in 5 steps following the 00SI/00SC route named first by the source, made uniform by the conormal identification of the source's second proof: (1) presentation S = k[x]/I, I finitely generated (P Noetherian), base change S' = K[x]/I' with I' = I K[x] (existing Mathlib leaf presentation-base-change), giving finite type; (2) I'/I'^2 = I/I^2 (x)_S S' as S'-modules, proved from the exactness of - (x)_k K (existing leaf lem-weil-field-scalar-extension-exact) and k[x] (x)_k K = K[x] (the source cites 00S4, NL base change; only its H_{-1}-level piece is needed); (3) dim at a point preserved (new node, 00P4), localization and fibre identities of the conormal modules; (4) only if: 00SC (1)=>(4) (existing node lci-conormal-free-rank-codimension) at p, transported to q, then 00SC (3)=>(1) (new node) over K; (5) if: a prime q over every p (existing node spec-surjective-base-change, Spec K -> Spec k surjective), 00SC (1)=>(4) over K, fibre dimension count and Nakayama (existing leaf) give n - d generators of (I/I^2)_p, then 00SC (3)=>(1) over k. Working at all primes avoids the Nullstellensatz/finite-fibre argument of the source's second proof, and the regular-sequence/flatness route of its 'only if' paragraph. Two new unsplit nodes (00SC (3)=>(1); 00P4), searched with leansearch, leanfinder, loogle and grep: Mathlib has no complete intersections and no dimension at a point. The citer lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-local-complete-intersection uses the 'if' direction (step 5).

lean.statement: theorem isLocalCompleteIntersection_fieldChange (k : Type u) (K : Type v) (S : Type w) [Field k] [Field K] [CommRing S] [Algebra k K] [Algebra k S] [Algebra.FiniteType k S] : letI := Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (R := k) (A := S) (B := K) ∃ h : Algebra.FiniteType K (S ⊗[k] K), letI := h IsLocalCompleteIntersection k S ↔ IsLocalCompleteIntersection K (S ⊗[k] K)
